results.name: range_inclusion_gap
results.description: Among multi-example sets and targets not in the set, yes-rate for targets inside [min,max] of the examples minus yes-rate for targets outside; observed above model mean means people use numeric range/magnitude that the digit model ignores.
results.code:
# name: range_inclusion_gap
# description: Among multi-example sets and targets not in the set, yes-rate for targets inside [min,max] of the examples minus yes-rate for targets outside; observed above model mean means people use numeric range/magnitude that the digit model ignores.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    lo = np.nanmin(X, axis=1); hi = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    inset = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    base = (n >= 2) & ~inset
    ins = base & (t >= lo) & (t <= hi); out = base & ~((t >= lo) & (t <= hi))
    if not ins.any() or not out.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[ins].mean() - r[out].mean())

results.name: same_decade_boost_no_digit_match
results.description: Among targets not sharing a final digit with any example (and not in the set), yes-rate for targets sharing a tens digit (decade) with some example minus others; observed above model mean means the model misses leading-digit/decade similarity.
results.code:
# name: same_decade_boost_no_digit_match
# description: Among targets not sharing a final digit with any example (and not in the set), yes-rate for targets sharing a tens digit (decade) with some example minus others; observed above model mean means the model misses leading-digit/decade similarity.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    ten = np.floor(np.minimum(X, 99) / 10); tt = np.floor(np.minimum(t, 99) / 10)
    nodig = ~((X % 10) == (t[:, None] % 10)).any(axis=1)
    dec = (ten == tt[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    a = nodig & dec; b = nodig & ~dec
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: item_rate_variance
results.description: Variance across (set,target) items of the per-item yes-rate; observed above model mean means items differ more systematically than the model's three features can explain (unexplained stimulus structure).

def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)

    m = pd.Series(r).groupby(key.to_numpy()).mean()
    return float(m.var(ddof=0))

results.name: single_vs_multi_example_yes_gap
results.description: Overall yes-rate on single-example sets minus yes-rate on 3-4-example sets (targets not in set); observed differing from model mean means the model mis-captures how generalization breadth changes with number of examples (size principle).
results.code:
# name: single_vs_multi_example_yes_gap
# description: Overall yes-rate on single-example sets minus yes-rate on 3-4-example sets (targets not in set); observed differing from model mean means the model mis-captures how generalization breadth changes with number of examples (size principle).
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    inset = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    a = (n == 1) & ~inset; b = (n >= 3) & ~inset
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: proximity_corr_no_digit_match
results.description: Correlation between rating and -log(1+distance to nearest example) among targets sharing no final digit with any example; observed above model mean means numeric closeness drives yes beyond what the digit model predicts.
results.code:
# name: proximity_corr_no_digit_match
# description: Correlation between rating and -log(1+distance to nearest example) among targets sharing no final digit with any example; observed above model mean means numeric closeness drives yes beyond what the digit model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    nodig = ~((X % 10) == (t[:, None] % 10)).any(axis=1) & (dist > 0)
    x = -np.log1p(dist[nodig]); y = r[nodig]
    if len(y) < 3 or x.std() == 0 or y.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.corrcoef(x, y)[0, 1])

results.name: square_target_boost_in_square_sets
results.description: In sets where at least two examples are perfect squares (and >=half are), yes-rate on non-example perfect-square targets minus on non-square targets; observed above model mean means people infer a 'squares' rule the digit/common-factor model lacks.
results.code:
# name: square_target_boost_in_square_sets
# description: In sets where at least two examples are perfect squares (and >=half are), yes-rate on non-example perfect-square targets minus on non-square targets; observed above model mean means people infer a 'squares' rule the digit/common-factor model lacks.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    sq = lambda a: np.isclose(np.round(np.sqrt(np.nan_to_num(a))) ** 2, np.nan_to_num(a))
    nsq = (sq(X) & valid).sum(axis=1)
    sset = (nsq >= 2) & (nsq * 2 >= n)
    inset = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    ts = sq(t)
    a = sset & ~inset & ts; b = sset & ~inset & ~ts
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: prime_target_boost_in_prime_sets
results.description: In sets with >=2 examples, all prime, yes-rate on non-example prime targets minus odd non-prime targets; observed above model mean means people infer a 'primes' rule that the digit model (which only sees final digit/parity) misses.
results.code:
# name: prime_target_boost_in_prime_sets
# description: In sets with >=2 examples, all prime, yes-rate on non-example prime targets minus odd non-prime targets; observed above model mean means people infer a 'primes' rule that the digit model (which only sees final digit/parity) misses.
def test_statistic(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(X)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    def isprime(a):
        a = np.nan_to_num(a).astype(int)
        out = a >= 2
        for p in (2, 3, 5, 7):
            out &= ~((a % p == 0) & (a != p))
        return out
    allp = ((isprime(X) | ~valid).all(axis=1)) & (n >= 2)
    inset = (X == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    tp = isprime(t); odd = (t.astype(int) % 2 == 1)
    a = allp & ~inset & tp; b = allp & ~inset & ~tp & odd
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())
